deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Protects against accidental deletion of the VPN tunnel via Terraform. Policy will whitelist "PREVENT" so the tunnel can't be destroyed unintentionally.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: Free-text description field for human readability only; does not affect the tunnel's configuration or behaviour.

ike_version.description:
IKE protocol version to use when establishing the VPN tunnel with
peer VPN gateway.
Acceptable IKE versions are 1 or 2. Default version is 2.
ike_version.rationale: IKEv1 is older and weaker than IKEv2. Policy will whitelist version 2 to enforce the stronger protocol.

labels.description:
Labels to apply to this VpnTunnel.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Key/value metadata for organisation and billing; does not affect the tunnel's security configuration.

local_traffic_selector.description:
Local traffic selector to use when establishing the VPN tunnel with
peer VPN gateway. The value should be a CIDR formatted string,
for example '192.168.0.0/16'. The ranges should be disjoint.
Only IPv4 is supported.
local_traffic_selector.rationale: Traffic selector defining which local networks are offered to the peer during IKE negotiation. Which networks a team chooses to expose over a given tunnel is a network design decision specific to that deployment, and access between the connected networks is enforced by firewall rules rather than by the selector itself, so there is no generic secure value to enforce.

name.description:
Name of the resource. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and
comply with RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63
characters long and match the regular expression
'[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the first character
must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must
be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit,
except the last character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: Just a naming/display identifier, no effect on the resource's security posture.

peer_external_gateway.description: URL of the peer side external VPN gateway to which this VPN tunnel is connected.
peer_external_gateway.rationale: Connectivity reference to the peer gateway resource, not itself a configurable security control.

peer_external_gateway_interface.description: The interface ID of the external VPN gateway to which this VPN tunnel is connected.
peer_external_gateway_interface.rationale: Selects which interface index on the peer gateway is used; a connectivity detail, not a security control.

peer_gcp_gateway.description:
URL of the peer side HA GCP VPN gateway to which this VPN tunnel is connected.
If provided, the VPN tunnel will automatically use the same vpn_gateway_interface
ID in the peer GCP VPN gateway.
This field must reference a 'google_compute_ha_vpn_gateway' resource.
peer_gcp_gateway.rationale: Identifier referencing an existing HA VPN gateway resource. We do not constrain what a resource points at; the referenced gateway is secured by its own policies.

peer_ip.description: IP address of the peer VPN gateway. Only IPv4 is supported.
peer_ip.rationale: Identifier for the external peer VPN gateway endpoint. A platform policy cannot pin a specific external address without knowing the deployment, and we do not constrain references to entities outside this resource.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies which GCP project the resource belongs to; an administrative reference, not a security control.

region.description: The region where the tunnel is located. If unset, is set to the region of 'target_vpn_gateway'.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

remote_traffic_selector.description:
Remote traffic selector to use when establishing the VPN tunnel with
peer VPN gateway. The value should be a CIDR formatted string,
for example '192.168.0.0/16'. The ranges should be disjoint.
Only IPv4 is supported.
remote_traffic_selector.rationale: Traffic selector defining which peer networks the tunnel will accept during IKE negotiation. It reflects what the two sides have agreed to route between them, which varies per deployment, and traffic reaching those networks is controlled by firewall rules rather than by the selector, so a platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain it.

router.description: URL of router resource to be used for dynamic routing.
router.rationale: References which Cloud Router handles dynamic routing for this tunnel; an operational/architecture choice, not a security control.

shared_secret.description:
Shared secret used to set the secure session between the Cloud VPN
gateway and the peer VPN gateway.
shared_secret.rationale: This is the pre-shared credential securing the IKE session, equivalent to a password. Policy should ensure it is set and not left blank or trivially weak.

shared_secret_wo.description:
Shared secret used to set the secure session between the Cloud VPN
gateway and the peer VPN gateway.
shared_secret_wo.rationale: Write-only variant of the IKE pre-shared key. Terraform never writes the value of a write-only argument into the plan output, so it appears as null regardless of what is configured. Since no value reaches the plan, there is nothing a policy can evaluate for this argument.

shared_secret_wo_version.description: Triggers update of 'shared_secret_wo' write-only. Increment this value when an update to 'shared_secret_wo' is needed. For more info see [updating write-only arguments](/docs/providers/google/guides/using_write_only_arguments.html#updating-write-only-arguments)
shared_secret_wo_version.rationale: Version identifier for the write-only shared secret, used by Terraform to detect that a new secret value has been supplied. It carries no secret material and sets no cryptographic standard, so there is no secure value a policy could enforce.

target_vpn_gateway.description:
URL of the Target VPN gateway with which this VPN tunnel is
associated.
target_vpn_gateway.rationale: Connectivity reference to the classic Target VPN Gateway this tunnel attaches to, not itself a security control.

vpn_gateway.description:
URL of the VPN gateway with which this VPN tunnel is associated.
This must be used if a High Availability VPN gateway resource is created.
This field must reference a 'google_compute_ha_vpn_gateway' resource.
vpn_gateway.rationale: Connectivity reference to the HA VPN gateway this tunnel attaches to, not itself a security control.

vpn_gateway_interface.description: The interface ID of the VPN gateway with which this VPN tunnel is associated.
vpn_gateway_interface.rationale: Selects which interface index on the VPN gateway is used; a connectivity detail, not a security control.

cipher_suite.description: User specified list of ciphers to use for the phase 1 and phase 2 of the IKE protocol.

cipher_suite.phase1.description: Cipher configuration for phase 1 of the IKE protocol.

cipher_suite.phase1.dh.rationale: Diffie-Hellman group used in IKE phase 1 key exchange. Policy will blacklist weak/legacy groups to enforce strong key exchange.

cipher_suite.phase1.encryption.rationale: Encryption algorithm used in IKE phase 1. Policy will blacklist weak ciphers (e.g. DES, 3DES) to enforce strong encryption.

cipher_suite.phase1.integrity.rationale: Integrity/hashing algorithm used in IKE phase 1. Policy will blacklist weak algorithms (e.g. MD5, SHA1) to enforce strong integrity checking.

cipher_suite.phase1.prf.rationale: Pseudo-random function used in IKE phase 1 key derivation. Policy will blacklist weak PRFs to enforce strong key derivation.

cipher_suite.phase2.description: Cipher configuration for phase 2 of the IKE protocol.

cipher_suite.phase2.encryption.rationale: Encryption algorithm used in IKE phase 2 (data channel). Policy will blacklist weak ciphers to enforce strong encryption of tunnel traffic.

cipher_suite.phase2.integrity.rationale: Integrity/hashing algorithm used in IKE phase 2. Policy will blacklist weak algorithms to enforce strong integrity checking of tunnel traffic.

cipher_suite.phase2.pfs.rationale: Perfect Forward Secrecy group for phase 2. Policy will blacklist weak/legacy groups so past sessions stay protected even if a key is later compromised.

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the Vpn Tunnel. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id},
and values are in the format tagValues/456.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Binds resource manager tags to the tunnel at creation time. The params block is passed with the API request but is not persisted as part of the resource payload, so the tag values never appear in the Terraform plan and cannot be evaluated. Which tags a team applies is also a governance labelling choice specific to their org hierarchy rather than a value a generic platform policy could constrain.
